data.name: Trijal
data.gender_notes: Trijal is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Trijal is derived from the Sanskrit language and is a masculine name. It is a compound name made up of the prefix tri, meaning three, and the suffix jal, meaning battle or victory. In Hindu mythology, Trijal is believed to be a warrior name, symbolizing the strength and courage of a victor in three battles. The name Trijal carries the meaning “Victorious in Three Battles” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Trijal usually hope their child will grow to embody victorious in three battles and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Emblematic of courage and perseverance in the face of adversity.

historical_references.reference:
Trijal was a renowned Jain scholar from Karnataka, India, who lived during the 12th century. He was a disciple of Hemachandra, the 11th century Jain scholar and founder of the Digambara Terapanthi sect.
Context: Trijal played a significant role in the development of Jain philosophy, particularly in the areas of metaphysics and ethics.

Trijal's works include commentaries on the Agama texts and the Nyaya Sutras, as well as original compositions such as the Tattvartha Sutra commentary and the Siddhanta Ratna.
Context: These works helped to solidify the Digambara Terapanthi tradition and influenced later Jain thinkers.
